title: Tojo sentenced to hang

facts.text: On 12 November 1948, the International Military Tribunal for the Far East in Tokyo handed down its sentences on Japan's wartime leaders.
Seven men were sentenced to death by hanging, among them Gen. Hideki Tojo, Japan's prime minister during the war.
The others condemned to die were Kenji Doihara, Koki Hirota, Seishiro Itagaki, Heitaro Kimura, Akira Muto, and Iwane Matsui.
Sixteen defendants were sentenced to life in prison, and two received prison terms: 20 years for Shigenori Togo and 7 for Mamoru Shigemitsu.
The court had first sat in April 1946. Over two and a half years it heard 419 witnesses and took in 4,336 exhibits.
Eleven judges sat, from nations that had fought Japan. The president was Sir William Webb of Australia, who read out the long judgment from 4 to 12 November 1948.
The court sat at Ichigaya in Tokyo, in a building that had belonged to the Imperial Japanese Army.
Emperor Hirohito was never charged or called to testify.
The seven condemned men were hanged at Sugamo Prison on 23 December 1948.
An Army Signal Corps camera filmed the final session, with a slate marking the date, 12 November 1948.

photoNote: Sir William Webb, president of the tribunal, reads the judgment from the bench under the flags of the Allied nations, Tokyo, 12 November 1948. A still frame (at 5:00 of the reel) from U.S. Army Signal Corps film 111-ADC-7423 (NARA 21195), whose slate dates it 12 November 1948; public domain. Standard definition film (720 x 480, 4:3), scaled to 1280 x 960, so it will look soft. No public domain photo of Tojo in the dock on the day was found: the well known color portrait on Commons traces to Bettmann (Getty), and the Truman Library photos of Tojo are marked copyright undetermined, so they were not used.

declassified.fact: Not every judge agreed. Justice Radhabinod Pal of India wrote a long dissent arguing that every defendant should be acquitted on every charge.
